Everything looks correct. Here is a complete account of what was created and edited.

---

## What was created and edited

### Files created

**`server/src/http/types.ts`** (new, 35 lines)

Defines the three core transport-agnostic types:

- `ActorContext` (line 5) — the normalized subset of the Express actor shape, only for authenticated actors (`"board" | "agent"`). The `"none"` case from `express.d.ts` is represented as `null` on `RequestCtx.actor` instead.
- `RequestCtx` (line 13) — the minimal normalized request interface. `json<T>()`, `text()`, `param()`, `query()` are all methods so callers never touch transport primitives directly. `db` and `storage` are always present here; the optional-db case in health is handled in the route layer.
- `Handler` (line 28) — `(ctx: RequestCtx) => Promise<Response>`. Uses the Web API `Response` type so handlers are portable to Hono/Workers.
- `RouteDefinition` (line 30) — carry type for future route registration tables.

**`server/src/http/express-adapter.ts`** (new, 113 lines)

`expressHandler(handler, deps)` at line 23 does five bridging jobs:

1. URL construction (line 29-31): builds `new URL(req.originalUrl, baseUrl)` from `req.hostname` + `req.protocol`.
2. Actor normalization (line 34-43): maps `req.actor.type === "none"` → `null`; copies only the four fields defined in `ActorContext`.
3. Header bridging (line 47-57): iterates `req.headers` (already lowercased by Node's HTTP parser) into a Web `Headers` object; handles `string[]` multi-value headers via `append`.
4. Body bridging (line 66-72): `json()` returns `req.body` directly (already parsed by `express.json()`); `text()` JSON-serialises if body is not already a string. No re-parsing.
5. Response forwarding (line 98-108): copies `response.status`, iterates `response.headers` (skipping `transfer-encoding` and `content-length` which Express manages), then sends via `res.send()`. Errors fall through to `next(err)`.

**`server/src/http/index.ts`** (new, 2 lines)

Barrel re-export of all four types and `expressHandler`.

---

### Files modified

**`server/src/routes/health.ts`** — all existing behavior preserved, zero behavior change in `app.ts`:

- Added imports (lines 11-13): `expressHandler`, `Handler`, `StorageService`.
- Extracted `buildHealthHandler(db, opts): Handler` (line 39-151) — a private factory that closes over the optional `db` and the deployment `opts`. The handler body is a verbatim port of the old `router.get("/", async (req, res) => { ... })` body, with three mechanical substitutions:
  - `req.actor?.type` → `ctx.actor?.type ?? null` (line 50)
  - `req.get("x-paperclip-dev-server-status-token")` → `ctx.headers.get("x-paperclip-dev-server-status-token") ?? undefined` (line 54)
  - `res.json(...)` / `res.status(N).json(...)` → `return Response.json(..., { status: N })` (lines 57-149)
- `healthRoutes(db?, opts?)` (line 160) — signature is byte-for-byte identical to the original. Internally it calls `buildHealthHandler`, supplies Proxy-based sentinels for `db` (when undefined) and `storage` (never needed), and wires them to `expressHandler` on `router.get("/")` (line 195-201). The existing `app.ts:183` mount (`api.use("/health", healthRoutes(...))`) requires no changes.
